name: Sheffield

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme in force. The London Road, Abbeydale Road and Chesterfield Road scheme ended on 31 October 2023, and the earlier Page Hall scheme ran from 2014 to 2019.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme. HMOs with five or more people from two or more households need a mandatory licence, whatever the number of floors.

housing: Sheffield is a hilly city of Victorian stone and brick terraces, large Victorian villas in the south-west, and big post-war council estates. Two universities mean a large student rental market, in shared houses around Broomhill, Crookes and Walkley and in purpose-built blocks in the city centre. The city still has a large council housing stock, though the private rented share grew between 2011 and 2021. There is no selective or additional licensing at present, only mandatory HMO licensing.
checkinTips: Student shared houses in Broomhill, Crookes and Walkley: photograph each bedroom door lock, fire doors, smoke alarms and the shared kitchen, room by room.
Stone terraces on steep streets: record cellars, rear yards, steps, retaining walls and any damp on walls built into the hillside.
Victorian villas split into flats in Broomhall and Nether Edge: note which rooms, gardens and storage belong to the flat, and photograph the communal hall and meters.
Flats over shops on Abbeydale, London and Ecclesall Roads: photograph the fire escape route, smoke alarms and the street door.
Apartments in the city centre and Kelham Island: note fob, key and parking counts, the post box and bin store, and any marks on exposed brick or concrete.
Homes in Stocksbridge and the edge of the Peak District: check for damp, frost damage to outside pipes and the condition of gutters after winter.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact Sheffield City Council's private housing standards team, which inspects privately rented homes and enforces HMO licensing.
